topic_title: Determine the characteristics of jointly distributed random variables

mission.display_title: State conditions under which random variables are independent
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to make independence a testable condition on jointly distributed variables. So you can recognise when the joint factors and refuse treating 'uncorrelated' or 'looks separate' as independence without a warrant.
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will force the candidate to state an independence condition (joint = product of marginals, or equivalent) and refuse correlation-as-independence theatre.
mission.educational_intent: Produce discrimination between joint structure and lawful independence conditions.
mission.learning_objective: State and apply the conditions under which random variables are independent.
mission.concept_focus: Independence condition → check on joint/marginals → refuse uncorrelated-as-independent.
mission.prior_bridge: Yesterday you obtained marginals and conditionals from a joint (2.2.1). Today tests when variables are independent.
mission.why_now: 2.2.2 is contiguous after marginals/conditionals; dependence measures (2.2.3) need this hinge.
mission.expected_benefit: Study Progress for independence conditions. Not covariance mastery.
mission.explainability: Campaign Epsilon Day 2 continues Continuity Front at LO 2.2.2.
success_criteria: Closed-book, state one independence condition in joint/marginal language.
Apply it to accept or reject independence on a simple sketch.
Refuse: 'uncorrelated means independent' without further warrant.
task_descriptions: Sketch the independence factorisation before CMP.
Knowledge Checks: condition + refuse correlation collapse.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.2.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. State one clear condition under which X and Y are independent, using joint and marginal language (or an equivalent CMP form).
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: X and Y are independent if the joint equals the product of the marginals (for all x,y in the support). Or an equivalent CMP statement (e.g. conditional equals marginal).
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 2.2.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. A student says 'correlation is zero, so they are independent.' Refuse and state what additional warrant independence requires.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Refuse: zero correlation is not independence. Independence requires the joint factorisation (or equivalent). Uncorrelated is weaker and can fail for non-linear dependence.
